notes.title: Power Up with New Buildings and Resource System Tweaks!
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone,[/p][p][/p][p]It’s been a bit over a month since the last update, and we’ve been working on another round of improvements.[/p][p][/p][p]After we introduced [b]a change to our resource depletion system in our last update[/b], we have gotten a lot of [b]feedback from the community[/b] that we have decided to address with a brand-new building type.
[/p][h3][u][b]Introducing: Power Plants[/b][/u][/h3][p]With [b]electricity slowly becoming the standard[/b] at the turn of the century, you’ll need to find ways to satisfy the demand and keep the ball rolling. That’s why we’ve added two brand-new building types to Railroad Corporation 2: [b]the Oil Power Plant and the Coal Power Plant[/b]. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/0d5ad84fe0bf5f675c22f5c2f30fa5f1c1289c8d.png"][/img][/p][p]With these new buildings, you’ll be able to produce electricity to sell to the greater population, or use it in your own production! The chemical factory, for example, now uses [b]electricity to produce chemicals that can be turned into dynamite in the Explosives factory[/b]. [/p][p]  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/9d72f58035ee2f39f6bc45ac78425fca1c0337a7.png"][/img] [/p][h3][u][b]More Resource Tools[/b][/u][/h3][p]But that’s not all: Electricity is the key to a variety of other renewable resources: Dynamite can be used to restore exhausted mines and electricity allows you to unearth even more layers of your clay pits. We’ve also increased the availability of oil in the oil well, but be mindful: the deeper you go, the higher your upkeep costs will be. [/p][p][/p][h3][u][b]Other Changes[/b][/u][/h3][p]As always, we’ve also included a handful of quality of life improvements! Competitive mode is now available for user-generated Multiplayer maps and we’ve also added resource capacity options for your lobbies. Additionally, trains will now move against the direction of a road if the path is defined before the semaphore has been switched.[/p][p]Finally, we’ve implemented a handful of Balancing and UI improvements. You can read our detailed [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1677970/view/562503219018728010"]patch notes here. [/url][/p][p][b][i]⚠️ Please note that, due to the significant changes made in this update, we've run into another (this time, smaller) issue when it comes to your save files. While post-mission save files will be still be compatible, those made during a mission will not. Just like last time, you'll still be able to access the previous version through a separate branch, to tie up any loose deals.[/i][/b][/p][p]We’d be curious to hear what you think about the new resource system! As always, we’ll be actively reading your comments on Discord and the Steam Discussion board.
[/p][p]See you soon,[/p][p]Corbie Games[/p]

notes.title: An Exciting New Update Rolls Into Railroad Corporation 2!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We hope you’ve all been enjoying your time on the rails, building networks, striking deals, and growing your corporation one station at a time!

Today, we’re excited to[b] bring you a brand-new update![/b] This one’s packed with exciting features, balancing improvements, and quality-of-life upgrades that we think will make your railroad adventures even more engaging.

[u][h5]New Features:[/h5][/u]
The [b]North Subjugation campaign has been expanded[/b] with a brand-new mission and [b]a full CEO skills system[/b]. You’ll also find a [b]Trading Department now available[/b] in your office, contracts for goods delivery, and a Finance Department overhaul that introduces loans, bonds, and a company credit rating system. More strategic depth? You got it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/b7175c4346f3787e6abbe87819e098d41bcd8960.png[/img]
When it comes to trains and infrastructure, we’ve added the [b]4-4-2 Atlantic locomotive[/b] to your research chart and introduced the [b]brand-new Chemical Plant as a production building[/b]. Oh, and there's now a [b]Trading Academy[/b] social building to boot.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/e44f48a8079064d0076a892b6b610e684e593f9f.png[/img]
We’ve also [b]rebalanced commodity pricing, mining resources, and multiplayer staffing[/b], among other adjustments to help the economic simulation feel even more dynamic and responsive.

And yes, there’s a whole wave of [b]UI upgrades, bug fixes, and localization improvements[/b] that should make your railroad empire a smoother ride.

[b][i]⚠️ Please note: This update comes with a full save wipe due to major system changes. But don’t worry—if you want to finish up your current playthrough first, the old version is still available on a separate branch.[/i][/b]

You can check out the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1677970/view/505078875556937859]full patch notes[/url] for all the details. As always, thanks for being part of our journey. We can’t wait to hear what you think of the new additions!

notes.title: Catch Our 6 Month Early Access Overview on YouTube!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

It’s already been [b]six months since Railroad Corporation 2 launched into Early Access[/b] back in October 2024, and we thought it’d be the perfect time to look back at what has happened so far. A bunch of exciting new additions have made it into the game, and [b]our friends at Iceberg Interactive have prepared an overview video, showing off some of the features of the last 6 months[/b]. 

[previewyoutube=26mJu6WDgpY;full][/previewyoutube]

In December, the [b]Autumn Biome[/b] was released, giving you the option of trading the snowy peaks of the winter biome for greener pastures. The new biome came with a variety of new maps with a variety of different playstyles:
 [list]
[*] [b]Autumn Journey[/b], a new, larger sandbox map. 
[*] [b]Nature of Competition[/b], a competitive 2-4 player map, where you can challenge your friends and see who can build the most successful railroad corporation.
[*] [b]Mutual Fund[/b], a cooperative multiplayer map. Instead of competing against your friends, you now have to work together to expand your corporation’s reach!
[/list]
Two months later, we added [b]Generated Scenarios[/b]. You can now [b]generate your own map, with the ability to tweak details according to your preference[/b]. Generated scenarios allow you to modify your terrain, add or remove raw materials, choose your objectives and much more - both in single- and multiplayer sessions.

Along with these big additions, there’s been [b]a variety of other notable fixes and improvements[/b] throughout the last six months. We updated semaphores, which you can now freely place on the entirety of your track by [b]Shift + Left click[/b], allowing for a much smoother way to get multiple trains to use your tracks. The [b]tax system[/b] has also been implemented, adding some difficulty to the game by having to pay taxes every year over the money you’ve made with your corporation. 

There’s a slew of other changes that you can review by reading our previous blogs or our changelog. Early Access has been an incredibly exciting time and we can’t wait to see where this journey takes us.
[h3]
We have a big update, with a bunch of exhilarating features, coming soon, so stay tuned! Can’t wait to see your reactions.[/h3]

Corbie Games

notes.title: Customize Your Sessions With Generated Scenarios!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello everyone,[/h3]

It’s been a while since we dropped our last Early Access update back in December! We’ve been working hard over the past few months and we’re super excited about the slew of features we’re sharing with you today.

We know that some of you have probably already explored every inch of our pre-made maps. Well, we have good news: [b]you’ll now be able to create your very own, user-generated landscapes! [/b]

[h4][u][b]Generated Scenarios: Craft Your Own Single- and Multiplayer Sessions[/b][/u][/h4]

Start your railroad career on your own, uniquely customized maps! You can [b]define your biome & terrain type, choose the size of your map & toggle the availability of certain raw materials[/b]. You can further customize your experience by [b]setting your starting capital and handpicking the amount of commodity objectives[/b] in any given game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/26b1faf05440e70923dade79049abc92ba3ad6f9.png[/img]
Generated scenarios are also available in [b]Multiplayer[/b], meaning that you can create unique challenges for you and your friends. Any scenario you generate comes with a [b]unique Random seed, that can be freely saved & shared! [/b]

[h4][u][b]Balancing & other fixes[/b][/u][/h4]

As with any update, the [b]updated version comes with a range of fixes[/b]. We made some improvements to the [b]UI[/b] and [b]fixed a variety of bugs[/b] that some of you reported! We’ve also improved the [b]balancing on some of the trains[/b] and added [b]level requirements[/b] in the lobbying department. We’ve also introduced a feature where warehouses can now be used by multiple players in Multiplayer co-op games! 

If you want to read a detailed breakdown of our new features, improvements, and fixes, you can consult the full patch notes [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1677970/discussions/0/4699035743124830016/]here[/url].

As always, [b]a heartfelt thank you goes out to the community[/b] for your ongoing support and insightful feedback. Your enthusiasm for the game inspires us to evolve with every new update! We can’t wait to hear what you think of the new scenario generator! As for us, we are starting to work on the next patch. :)

Patch 0.8.12156: Autumn biome & 3 new maps
notes.content:
We’re thrilled to share the latest update for the game! This time, we’re introducing [b]the Autumn Biome (A.K.A. the "green biome") with three brand-new maps. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/17c7de6689c8250172a25b34e360018c940ddd4a.png[/img]

[u][b]Autumn Journey[/b][/u]
A single-player endless mode with no objectives, designed for creative exploration and experimentation. This map is larger than the ‘Frozen Lakes’ map you’ve gotten to know so well by now.

[u][b]Nature of Competition[/b][/u]
A competitive 2-4 player versus map with specific objectives focused on managing and delivering certain commodities.

[u][b]Mutual Fund[/b][/u]
A cooperative multiplayer map that illustrates a collaborative plan to fund and develop a railroad network in a resource-rich area, addressing regulatory requirements and shared risks.

We do advise players to play the Frozen Lakes or Northern Subjugation maps first as those include vital tutorial elements explaining core mechanics. 

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[u][b]Why an Autumn Biome in Winter?[/b][/u]

We’ve received numerous requests for an alternative to the winter biome since our Early Access release. To accommodate this, we prioritized the Autumn Biome earlier in our roadmap.
And yes, we know it’s winter, so releasing an autumn-themed update might seem...unexpected. Think of it as a cozy warm-up to the snowier adventures ahead!

The Autumn Biome sets the stage for new main campaign chapters that will be created using this new biome.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[u][b]Key Features in the Update[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] [b]Larger Sandbox Map:[/b] Autumn Journey offers more space to explore than Frozen Lakes. However, we still encourage new players to start with Frozen Lakes or Northern Subjugation, since they offer a clear introduction to the mechanics of Railroad Corporation 2
[*] [b]New Versus Map Objectives:[/b] Multiplayer objectives now emphasize specific commodities, adding a fresh layer of strategic challenge.
[*] [b]New Cooperative Map:[/b] Large cooperative map with a variety of challenges. Great for co-op players who already have some experience in Railroad Corporation 2.
[/list]
[b]Improvements and Fixes[/b]
Here's a list of all changes and improvements. As always, you can also follow the change log [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1677970/discussions/0/4699035743124830016/]over on our Steam discussions thread. [/url]

Patch change log:

Content
    - Added three new maps set in a brand-new Autumn biome.

Balancing
    - Adjusted research values for the Mason Bogie locomotive.
    - Large bakery stores are now allowed to be constructed.

Fixes
    - Resolved an issue where multiplayer sessions could not be loaded after geology succeeded.
    - Fixed a bug where newly created cities were missing a City Hall in some cases.
    - Addressed an issue where not all commodities were visible in the Warehouse panel.
    - Corrected a problem where trains occasionally failed to leave a station without an obvious reason.

notes.title: Developer Log 8 - Company Reports
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We’re back with another blog today and we’d like to showcase a small but crucial new addition to [i]Railroad Corporation 2[/i]: Company Reports!

Company reports offer a comprehensive overview of your corporation's performance. Let's delve into each tab of the reports section to understand their significance.

[h3][u]Overview[/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/e30e2494a950398b0db8f4448b7e295dfe71bb73.png[/img]
Starting with the Overview Tab, this tab serves as the control hub for your corporation. It presents key information at a glance, including your current cash reserves and outstanding debt. You'll also find a summary of your property holdings, such as buildings and locomotives, essential assets for expanding your operations. Additionally, the overview tab offers insights into the extent of your railway network, showcasing the mileage of tracks you've laid out. Furthermore, you'll have access to details about the manager you've hired, including their specialty and costs.

[h3][u]Balance Sheet[/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/593d49a928660d486622cf5fae85f5d9ac9110b1.png[/img]
In the Balance Sheet tab, you'll dive deeper into the financial health of your corporation. It provides a breakdown of your assets and liabilities, allowing you to assess your company's overall worth. By comparing year-to-date figures with historical data, you can track the trajectory of your financial standing and identify trends that may impact your strategic decisions.

[h3][u]Profit and Loss[/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/6f33b0c24888e8b945fa874f02aabebadfb102ae.png[/img]
The Profit and Loss tab is where you monitor the financial performance of your corporation in detail. It records your revenue from various sources, including raw material purchases and sales, and transportation income. Simultaneously, it tracks your expenditures, such as operating costs, maintenance expenses, and employee wages. By analyzing these figures over different time frames, you gain a comprehensive understanding of your company's profitability and operational efficiency.

[h3][u]Transaction Log[/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/e0419e22526e4e9a2e7fc2cbd40f6c4ca0dc4709.gif[/img]
The Transaction Log tab acts as a ledger, providing a comprehensive record of all your financial transactions. Every purchase and sale within your corporation, from acquiring new locomotives to selling surplus resources, is documented here. The log uses a color-coded system to differentiate between income-generating activities (highlighted in green) and expenses (highlighted in red), enabling you to quickly assess the financial impact of each transaction.

[h3][u]Graphs[/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/160d36b10a8b9438a5cfa8559cab67ed19328fa6.png[/img]
In the Graphs tab, you'll find visual representations of your corporation's financial performance. The Net Profit graph illustrates the trend of your profits over time, allowing you to identify periods of growth or decline.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/f3463e166bf71bc52c0e375aecf5a5fd5b88bf35.png[/img]
Meanwhile, the Asset Balance graph tracks the total value of your company's assets, providing insights into your wealth accumulation and asset allocation strategies. These graphs offer intuitive visualizations that complement the detailed numerical data presented in other sections of the Company Reports.

That concludes today's update! We hope you find these company reports valuable as you step into the world of Railroad Corporation 2. Let us know what you think about this update on Steam’s Discussion Board, or Discord, and stay tuned for more updates!

Thank you for your ongoing support and enthusiasm!

notes.title: Developer Log 7 - Implementing New Special View Modes
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

In this developer log, we're excited to introduce one of the new features that were inspired by your community feedback: Special View Modes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/6ce6149cd506d6042d5f09ebf5902244cdfe991b.png[/img]
This feature will bring you enhanced tools to keep an overview and organise your railroad tracks effortlessly. This will let you pinpoint exact areas where on your tracks still require electrification, as well as identify areas for track optimization with greater ease.

[u][h3]Electrification View[/h3][/u] During the Alpha Demo, we noticed that some players had encountered some challenges when attempting to electrify entire railroad networks. In response, we've developed a special view mode specifically tailored to help players identify segments of the track that have not yet been electrified. So, in case you’ve missed a certain segment of the track, the electrification view will have your back.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/af3366675c0d1bf7a97d7b4cb6e3e3012b40ae0d.png[/img]
[i]Railroad track with a small segment without electricity.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/6b951e8face533de929f97b7b98327c6cf0d74a7.png[/img]
[i]Blue highlights the electrified railroad track, while red highlights railroad tracks without electricity.[/i]

Moreover, we’ve added in a new status for electrical locomotives: they will now be able to alert you when it cannot reach its destination because there isn't a fully electrified path available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/2dcacc86bf325c3a9aa52bd305464ca7d034e41d.png[/img]

[u][h3]Height View[/h3][/u] In addition to this electrification view mode, a special height mode has been implemented. This makes it easier to check elevation on your railroad layout and see where a slope or a drop have been created.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/b39d4f467660aedd86b0da3f9ab393062d7d21dd.png[/img]
Tracks highlighted in green denote ground-level tracks, while blue tracks signify those below ground level. Yellow tracks indicate the first level above ground, while red indicates the second level above ground, which is the highest level within Railroad Corporation 2. So, if your train seems to be moving unusually slowly, you can use the height view to see if the train’s slowness is caused by a change in elevation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/1285cc5e1c2c7d48bfed4d65fbdee7982d11994a.png[/img]
And that concludes our update for today! We're making steady progress on Railroad Corporation 2, and we're eager to share more of the game with you soon! For those who missed the alpha demo, don't worry – there will be another opportunity for you to try it out later. 

Thank you for your continued support and enthusiasm, let us know what you think on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1677970/discussions/]Steam’s Discussion Board[/url], or in [url=https://discord.gg/sbnGEcMz]Discord[/url], and stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Developer Log 5 - Development Process behind Steam Locomotive’s Exhaust
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We are back with another developer deep-dive, we delve into the intriguing subject of "Steam locomotive exhaust." The color and intensity of locomotive exhaust can vary significantly, prompting us to explore the factors influencing these variations. Our aim is to portray the railroad environment in a realistic manner within the constraints of our capabilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/c42c536ccf273f89859a1d2934d09024591a11bb.gif[/img]

Locomotive exhausts comprise two main components, namely smoke and steam, blended in varying proportions. Smoke originates from the combustion of wood, coal, or oil, the widely adopted fuels during the game's time period. Beyond impurities, the combustion products include carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and carbon itself. Of these, carbon dioxide is deemed the most “useful” due to its superior thermal energy output during the transformation of carbon from the fuel.

Carbon monoxide, on the other hand, arises when there is insufficient oxygen in the combustion chamber. This not only results in a partial waste of thermal energy but also poses a health hazard, earning it the non-scientific term "choke gas". Pure carbon represents wasted fuel, unable to find its air particle and contributing to the black color of smoke.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/698edf39e63c0e2c3fd5f6aede0d21c86af3f2c2.gif[/img]

A perfectly burnt fuel under ideal conditions should yield invisible smoke, while white smoke may indicate the presence of water in the burnt fuel. Now, turning our attention to steam, it serves as a medium for transporting the thermal energy generated by the combustion of fuel in the locomotive's firebox to the pistons.

The process involves burning fuel in the combustion chamber, heating water in the locomotive, and creating steam through boiling. This steam then powers the locomotive's pistons, turning its wheels. The color of steam is consistently white, and it is released from the smokestack when the locomotive is in motion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/deb41160583b3d9ccc33947eff9a97162737f555.gif[/img]

Examining the interplay between smoke and steam, we observe that the exhaust's color can range from white to black. A lighter color indicates more steam release and/or better fuel combustion, while a darker color signifies less steam release and/or inferior fuel combustion. Additionally, the exhaust's transparency, not previously discussed, depends on external weather conditions, primarily air temperature and humidity.

To better illustrate these concepts, we have provided links to YouTube videos showcasing actual locomotive exhaust phenomena:
[list]
[*] [url=https://youtu.be/CUlJzfQ-Blc?t=2m14s]3 Shay Locomotives[/url]
[*] [url=https://youtu.be/SMeRwbkoxqo?t=23s]William Mason Locomotive[/url]
[*] [url=https://youtu.be/5MnDBhzMc7Q?t=4m42s]'Eureka' Baldwin class 8-18 Locomotive[/url]
[*] [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sh0Dg5H5fs0&t=117s]Santa Maria Valley 205[/url]
[/list]
Analyzing provided examples, such as those in the given YouTube links, we not only witness changes in color but also variations in transparency. In brief, the transparency of exhaust is influenced by external factors, with dry summer days making it challenging to observe any exhaust, while wet and cold winter or autumn days facilitate clearer visibility due to steam condensation in the air.

And that’s all for our deep-dive into today’s blog! We hope you found this exploration of steam locomotive exhaust both informative and engaging. Stay tuned for more news and any announcements, and join our [url=https://discord.gg/Ab6dKzzj]Discord[/url] if there are any specific topics you’d like us to cover!

notes.title: Developer Log 4 - Designing Locomotives in Railroad Corporation 2
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We’re back again with another dev log today, and we’ll be covering the core feature in the game: Locomotives in Railroad Corporation 2.

If you've been with us since Railroad Corporation 1, you're likely familiar with the concept: you’ll need to purchase locomotives, each consisting of a single engine, to transport goods and carriages from one city to the next. Initially, only a small handful of locomotive models are available, but as you progress and complete research, new and advanced models unlock for you to add to your arsenal.

Now, in Railroad Corporation 2, we propel ourselves ahead in time, embracing innovations that pave the way for the emergence of new locomotives. As highlighted on the store page, the game primarily unfolds in the early 20th century, an era marked by the advent of electrification, which influenced the locomotives during this time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/bd9c45c10239eab51ea23da912e962f336d6435d.gif[/img]
In Railroad Corporation 2, our aim is to bring realism closer towards Railroad Corporation 2, and the in-game design of locomotives is no exception. Each locomotive model is heavily inspired and crafted based on schematics and properties sourced from reliable online references. Thus, we'd like to provide a walkthrough from schematics to the in-game model, using a locomotive example that we showcased in our last dev log that’ll be featured in Railroad Corporation 2: the 4-8-0 Mastodon steam locomotive!

Firstly, all locomotives within the game are based on design schematics found in online sources or handbooks, which serve as the starting point for the locomotive's design, capturing its details and specifications. Taking the 4-8-0 Mastodon steam locomotive as an example, its design blueprint was drawn from The Norfolk & Western Handbook by Wallace and Wiley, as well as inspired from other online sources.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/15f46db46dff7281e7a3467d6faf3d83d19431a3.png[/img]
[i]Wikimedia Commons - A. Bucher: Das Eisenbahnwesen auf der Weltausstellung in Brüssel 1910. in Polytechnisches Journal, S. 344, Fig. 143[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/033baa363ec7495021302eb4ec3d2419e8cd488a.jpg[/img]
[i]Wikimedia Commons - 1922 Locomotive Cyclopedia of American Practice[/i]

Next, our development team translates the blueprints into a fully realized 3D model, ensuring the dimensions and the core elements are reflected in-game. With the 4-8-0 Mastodon, the visual design of this locomotive is based on the Norfolk and Western M Class, a steam-powered behemoth crafted between 1906 and 1907 by Baldwin Locomotive Works and ALCO-Richmond Works.

Lastly, the technicalities and characteristics are programmed onto each of the locomotives based on their real-life counterpart’s statistics, which reflects how each type of locomotive will behave in-game, which includes details such as train power, tractive effort, maximum speed, locomotive mass, as well as its behavior on road slopes or turn curves, etc.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/5195be56e3eec501987bcd895b1173369d7b97a0.png[/img]
These properties collectively constitute a wealth of information that you must consider when evaluating each locomotive, aiding them in making informed decisions about the most suitable choice for various in-game situations:
[list]
[*] Top speed
[*] Max pulling mass
[*] Acceleration
[*] Reliability rate
[*] Rated mileage
[*] Service life
[*] Fuel conversion efficiency 
[/list]
In addition, there are other technical properties showcased in-game in how locomotives would react to different environments, as well as how each type of carriage would affect the performance of the locomotive in the form of graphic charts comparison.  

For example, the in-game graph below depicts how the nominal speed of a 4-8-0 Mastodon decreases based on both the slope of the terrain it traverses and the weight of its cargo.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/52f335122b8872782535c5c30b255edc0c7f9558.png[/img]

Armed with this information, you can effectively assess which locomotives align with your current requirements. Considerations such as the cargo's weight are essential, as well as factors like the characteristics of the locomotive’s itinerary. Whether you're dealing with short, direct tracks within a local agglomeration or a long-distance route traversing mountains with numerous curves, bridges, and slopes, evaluating locomotives in light of these details becomes crucial for optimal decision-making.

By incorporating these details, we aim to provide you with an immersive experience that stays true to its realism as you navigate the challenges of Railroad Corporation 2. 

And that wraps up today’s dev log. Thanks for your continued support, and stay tuned for more exciting developments as we continue to refine and enhance the world of Railroad Corporation 2!

notes.title: Railroad Corporation 2 - Devlog #2
notes.content:
After a certain pause we continue our Railroad Corporation 2 devlog, and today we would like to talk more about Corporation rather than Railroad. An essential part of any company is human resources. In Railroad Corporation 2 you will have to hire different specialists in different office departments, one of such departments is a geology department.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/30f3f17c2a4568a03c525e27c6626cb972e95d50.png[/img]

In Railroad Corporation 2, not all of the resources might be available for transportation right away, as some of them need to be discovered first. With help of the geology department you can plan your geology discoveries, hire necessary specialists and maintain studying of the terrain. 

Different department levels provide players with a certain information e.g. the probability of this or that resource to be found in a certain spot. Higher department levels offer more precise information about the terrain available. Of course, higher department levels will also influence your upkeep costs, so you'll have to manage your spending carefully.

Additionally a certain level of the department might be a requirement for hiring this or that specialist especially if the abilities of character are better than average. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/0c0ec6a3e6aec9df541c88c2143e049b6499d831.png[/img]

Geologists can be hired at a labor market. Each employee has a certain level as well, higher level means better impact on the geology department overall (passive skill) and on each particular discovery task (active skill). Specialists may affect different parameters, e.g. research speed, efficiency and cost of natural resources discovery. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/7d9083c179ccc65a2bc0f0b243d64f168109eee3.png[/img]

Each scenario map is split by blocks. Some blocks are not available for research, e.g. high mountains or lakes; others are discovery spots where geologists can be sent to run the research. 

Once a certain research is completed your specialists will require some rest. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/227b94b5eaedc1f773b0ac368f460a7547e9943a.png[/img]


During the research it is prohibited to perform any construction on site.

If a research is effective and natural resources are found it will be necessary to set up a city somewhere nearby the geology research site so you can set up a mine and railroad station to transport the resources. Of course, whoever found resources became the owner of those resources. This is an additional bonus from geological exploration.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/ddebb6f208d59151f2db7c5ba2f39aea2df42fcf.png[/img]

That’s all for now, but more news is coming. 
Stay tuned!

notes.title: Railroad Corporation 2 — Devlog #1
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

There are a lot of questions about what will be in Railroad Corporation 2, and the differences between it and the first game. So we'd like to take this opportunity to tell you about what's new in the sequel!

Today we're tackling the most vital game aspect - railroad construction.

In Railroad Corporation 2 we will keep the same logic of track building - you can lay tracks only from the existing track, but based on the player’s feedback we're making a lot of changes.

[h2]Crossing[/h2]
Yes, this time you will be able to make a track crossing! This was maybe the most frequent request about railroads and we couldn’t ignore it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/7b6ae1a49e4f2c36aaa7a29db5aba4857f1917ab.png[/img]

Diamond crossings are also an option!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/7af3ad1ef9887e423f4909808e8cc546a1435b0c.png[/img]

Moreover, you will be able to do multiple crossings. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/700876410e7bebc2865f710d030d70d8b160023e.png[/img]

[h2]Parallel Tracks[/h2]
Building of parallel tracks will be similar to Railroad Corporation 1 logic. You need to move the cursor to the existing track until a sign of the parallel track appears, click, and move along the existing track. We have improved snapping to the track, so building a parallel track will be easier. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/69161e176646177f98d5c8b79a877d9088304b72.gif[/img]

Moreover, crossing other tracks doesn’t cancel parallel track building. You can build a pretty long parallel track just in one click.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/729c31a6f07650d2ddda2b62b004aca9aa5e2d4e.gif[/img]

[h2]Bridges And Tunnels[/h2]
There will be 3 different bridges: wooden, steel and cement. They will have different speed limits and prices. And of course, it will be possible to build a bridge over existing tracks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/fb0012fdc1aa24f9a6a01a0f83b79010ece357a0.png[/img]

[h2]Junctions[/h2]
Junction logic remains the same, but again with more freedom. In Railroad Corporation 2 it will be possible to make a double junction. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/80319b6c90799cc0909d033c6b5cbe70680bd6b7.png[/img]

Even Scissor crossovers will be available in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41371493/3762d020d73ab4b605331718684884b0f1a751da.png[/img]

Thank you for reading! We're excited to share more news about Railroad Corporation 2 in the future, so stay tuned.
